test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 08 Sept, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following statements is true regarding quadrilaterals?

(i) A rhombus can be a square, but not all squares are rhombuses.

(ii) In a trapezium, two pairs of opposite sides are equal.

(iii) A rhombus is a special type of a parallelogram.

(iv) Diagonals are equal in parallelograms and rhombuses.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A **rhombus** is defined as a **parallelogram** with all four sides equal. Since it satisfies the property of having two pairs of parallel sides, it is classified as a special type of **parallelogram**. Therefore, statement (iii) is the only true statement.

**∴ The correct answer is iii.**
